one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 2 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with its expect line. Check 1 passes when loadConfig on bad JSON doesn't throw, exits 0 and prints `{} 0 true`, and when src/config.js's loadConfig "catches the JSON.parse error and returns {}". All of that restates line 1: it catches the error, returns {}, and sits in loadConfig in src/config.js. Extra stderr warnings are explicitly allowed. Check 2 asks only for exit 0 with no failing tests, which is what "npm test passes" means. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not a PASS/FAIL condition)": the test-file change, a missing file still throwing, the stderr warning that names the file, the README update and the app.js run. No mutation test, branch rule or exact wording appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Each file they use exists in the repo's six tracked files (src/config.js, src/app.js, test/config.test.js, README.md), and `npm test` maps to the "node --test" script. `printf '{port: 9000' > /tmp/...` has valid quoting and no format specifiers. `node --input-type=module -e "import { loadConfig } from './src/config.js'; ..."` is valid: with `-e`, relative imports resolve against the current directory, and the JS inside it parses. The missing-file check is also valid syntax. `npm install` only runs if dependencies exist, so it's safe. One thing I couldn't confirm: `node src/app.js /tmp/bad.json` assumes app.js takes the config path as an argument. That fits the brief's description of app.js and the issue, but I didn't see the file itself. I found no command that names a missing file, takes invalid arguments, or has broken shell or JS syntax.

catches-traps.why: Items 2 and 3 are met, but item 1 is not. Item 2: builder step 3 replaces 'bad JSON throws' with a test that the result is deepEqual to {}, and the context says that test "contradicts line 1 and must change". Item 3: verifier Check 1 calls loadConfig on `{port: 9000` and PASSes on `{} 0 true` with no throw. Item 1: no brief says, in a note or under Advisory, that line 1's fix hides the broken file, or that src/app.js would start on defaults instead of printing 'bad config'. The builder brief works around it by adding a stderr warning and updating the README to say the app "starts with the defaults". The verifier Advisory only asks to "Check whether the parse failure prints a warning… users need to know which file is broken". Both assume the problem without stating it.

avoids-must-not.why: Verifier brief: Check 1's PASS/FAIL conditions only require that the call returns {} (`{} 0 true`) and that the catch-and-return sits in loadConfig. It says "any extra stderr warning is fine", and the warning check appears only under "Advisory (not a PASS/FAIL condition)". So must_not item 1 is avoided. Builder brief: step 2 says "Inside the catch, before returning {}, write one line to stderr ... that names `path` and includes the parse error's message". That tells the builder to log a warning on a parse error in addition to returning {}. Must_not item 1 itself names logging a warning as asking for more than returning {}, so this goes past the issue's requirement and breaks must_not item 2. Step 4's README text about warning on stderr comes from the same instruction.

methods-private.why: I checked the builder brief for checks or probes that also appear in the verifier brief. Most of it is allowed. Step 5's `npm test` is named by expect line 2, and the test edits in step 3 are the builder writing its own tests. Step 5 also tells the builder to run `printf '{port: 9000' > /tmp/bad.json && node src/app.js /tmp/bad.json` and expect a stderr warning, `listening on 8080` and exit 0. The verifier brief's advisory list has the same probe: `printf '{port: 9000' > /tmp/v-bad.json && node src/app.js /tmp/v-bad.json` should print `listening on 8080` and exit 0. That is a probe with expected output, and no expect line or proof in the issue names it. Only the file path differs. Because the builder gets one of the checker's probes, the criterion breaks.
